tolerance_classes.EXACT_BYTES: files / serialized outputs byte-identical (sha256 equal); not used by this contract except where an observable says so
tolerance_classes.EXACT_VALUE: integers, strings, enums, booleans, statuses, error codes, schema shape, and floats that are copied (not computed): equal (floats compared by value, -0.0 == 0.0)
tolerance_classes.ULP_BOUNDED: |rust - py| <= k_ulp * ulp(py) OR |rust - py| <= r_rel * |py| OR |rust - py| <= a_abs, with k_ulp / r_rel / a_abs fixed per observable below (an absent clause is not applied). The relative clause is scaled by |py|, NOT by max(1, |py|) as in the template's proposal: the observables span 1e-12 .. 1e17, so an absolute floor of r_rel would accept nonsense for small quantities; scaling by |py| is strictly tighter for |py| < 1 and identical otherwise. ulp(py) = 2^(floor(log2|py|) - 52) (py = 0: smallest subnormal)
tolerance_classes.EXACT_STREAM: not used (no RNG in either implementation; the harness RNG only draws input vectors)

tolerance_basis.independence: fixed from an a priori floating-point analysis of the registered algorithms, before any Rust code or Python-vs-Rust comparison existed. Inputs of the analysis are properties of the frozen data and of the reference functions only: max |ln v| over the stored grid = 37.54 (n_O, ECSS_ST_HIGH); max |quiet wind| 253.6 m/s, max |disturbance wind| 575.1 m/s; Lebesgue constants of the registered weight functions over the domain (max sum |w|): doy 1.848, lst 1.848, lon 1.667, alt 1.459, lat 1.631; disturbance lat 1.631, lon 1.250, lst 1.250; np.loadtxt and Rust str::parse both give the correctly rounded doubles (checked on the reference side)
tolerance_basis.which_operations_differ: identical in both (expected bit-identical): CSV parsing; every IEEE basic operation evaluated in the same order (the theta argument of the trigonometric weights, the Lagrange and periodic-cubic weights, np.interp of the doy warp (X86_V2 baseline: no FMA), Python float remainder / floor-division, the _state_dict sums and ratios); glibc libm calls made by CPython math and Rust std alike (asin, atan2, sin, cos, sqrt, exp, log on scalars). Different: (i) numpy's AVX512 SIMD float64 log of the grid, exp of the result and cos inside the trigonometric weights (<= 4 ulp each, numpy's documented SIMD bound) against glibc (< 1 ulp); (ii) the summation order of the separable contractions (np.tensordot -> OpenBLAS dgemv, np.einsum) against Rust's sequential loop; (iii) np.linalg.norm (OpenBLAS ddot) against a sequential sum of squares
tolerance_basis.bound_log_interpolated: per axis a (order doy, alt, lat, lon, lst): D_a <= L_a D_(a-1) + sum_k |dw_k| X_a + 2 gamma_m L_a X_a with X_a = (prod_(b<a) L_b) * 37.54, gamma_m = m 2^-53, |dw_k| <= 9.3e-16 per trigonometric weight (5 ulp cos differences through w = (1 + 2 sum cos(k theta) + cos(m theta / 2)) / m) and 0 for Lagrange / periodic-cubic weights, D_0 = 5 ulp(37.54) = 3.55e-14: D_doy 4.8e-13, D_alt 7.9e-13, D_lat 1.4e-12, D_lon 3.7e-12, D_lst 9.8e-12; the final exp maps the absolute log difference to a relative one (+ 5 ulp): <= 1.0e-11 relative for rho, n_s, T; sums n_total <= 1.0e-11; ratios x_s <= 2.0e-11; flux = rho |v_rel| <= 1.0e-11 + 2 ulp
tolerance_basis.bound_wind: same recursion on linear values (no log / exp): quiet part (X_0 = 253.6 m/s, 5 axes) <= 6.2e-11 m/s; disturbance part (X_0 = 575.1 m/s; doy trigonometric, lat Lagrange, lon / lst periodic cubic) <= 2.3e-11 m/s; total <= 8.6e-11 m/s
tolerance_basis.bound_geometry: orbit geometry and DesignState.atm(): identical operations except the 3-term norm (<= 2 ulp)

registered.REL10 (log-interpolated fields and their: k_ulp 4 or r_rel 1e-10 (scale |py|): 5x above the a priori worst case for ratios (2.0e-11) and 5e3 below the 7-significant-digit storage resolution of the grid (5e-7)
registered.WIND (wind components): k_ulp 4 or a_abs 1e-9 m/s: 11x above the a priori worst case (8.6e-11 m/s) and 1e5 below the stored 1e-4 m/s resolution; absolute because wind components change sign

decision_rules.meaning_of_ADMITTED: A9.24 item 1: Rust becomes authoritative for this component (within the registered domain); new production results for it come from Rust and carry implementation = rust, rust_commit and this contract id; the Python component may then be retired from active execution. It is NOT physics validation.
decision_rules.no_retuning: tolerances, observables, inputs, n, seeds and rules are fixed; after NOT_ADMITTED only a code fix plus a new contract version with a fresh scoring_master_seed may follow; the failed report stays; no execution is discarded
